nodes.label: The Conductor (execution-quality persona)
nodes.rationale: Splits ownership deliberately: the engine decides which stage runs next and owns all lifecycle bookkeeping, while the conductor owns the irreducible knowledge-work of running that stage well. The persona is baked into the first directive of a session rather than referenced by path, so every entry point receives it identically.

nodes.label: Communication topologies (inline, subagent, pipeline, mob)
nodes.rationale: How support agents join is governed by directive.mode, never by the mere presence of support_agents, because the topology is who-talks-to-whom rather than who-participates. The conductor is the bus on every topology and agents never invoke each other, which keeps every inter-agent message an auditable dispatch. Mob runs as at most two bounded rounds with maintained dissent carried verbatim to the gate, so disagreement is never silently averaged away.

nodes.label: Collaborator contribution files as completion evidence
nodes.rationale: Everyone writes their own work and the owner collates: dispatched support agents write their own contribution files while the lead alone edits the produces[] artifacts, and the engine refuses approval while a declared collaborator's file is missing, which makes participation verifiable rather than asserted. It also lets resume re-dispatch only the missing spokes.

nodes.label: Stage observation diary (memory.md)
nodes.rationale: The diary is the only file the conductor maintains by hand; everything else (state fields, checkboxes, audit rows) is tool-owned. Creation is idempotent so a resume never loses accumulated entries, and it is left in place on approval because it is the stage's permanent record and the learnings gate reads it.

nodes.label: Walking-skeleton stance classification (gate: unresolved)
nodes.rationale: Most gate values are deterministic, but the first Construction Bolt depends on a stance no parser can derive from free-form practices prose, so the engine defers it as gate: unresolved, receives the classification back via report --skeleton-stance, and still owns the transition. Judgment is delegated; control is not.

nodes.label: PRACTICES_OVERRIDE judgement
nodes.rationale: When a bolt-plan marker and team practices disagree, practices wins and the divergence is recorded as an explicit override event, because practices are the team's standing voice while a bolt-plan marker is one workflow's interpretation.

nodes.label: Intra-stage control flow (Keep / Modify / Redo)
nodes.rationale: The clean split is between directives (the engine picks the next stage) versus within a stage (the conductor loops on its own); even so, every turn of the loop reports through the engine so the audit trail records the rejection and the revision rather than an invisible in-stage retry.
